text:
Recent work distinguishes genuine preference shifts from incidental interactions: [CoDeR+ (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3778863) models interest and demand drift explicitly, motivating checks of whether recent activity represents coherent intent or noise. [CETD (2023)](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176), an earlier methodological reference, emphasizes temporally structured, minimally changed counterfactual histories. These support perturbation-based diagnosis, but do not establish that sensitivity to deletion alone proves stale recurrent memory. The [original GRU4Rec implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/gru4rec) also distinguishes independent sessions from whole-history recommendation, where prediction depends on the state computed from preceding interactions.

Suggested training-only probe: hold out the next interaction from sampled training prefixes; compare intact histories against equal-count recent deletion, older deletion, matched random deletion, and local order shuffling. Keep candidate sets fixed across paired comparisons; match deletion counts and stratify by history length. Include shuffling that preserves the final item to separate order dependence from last-item dependence. Record target-rank change, HR@10 change, final-state cosine distance, and normalized state displacement. Repack surviving items chronologically and left-pad; verify readout selects the final nonpadding index, never count−1, and check invariance to added leading padding. Run the same trained GRU in evaluation mode for every condition. Report paired user-bootstrap confidence intervals, clustering multiple prefixes per user. Greater damage from recent deletion than matched controls suggests useful recency dependence; large state changes without rank changes suggest representational sensitivity without demonstrated predictive impact. Weak sensitivity can also reflect redundant histories, output scoring, or a padding bug. These are proposed diagnostics, not reported findings from the cited papers; leave official validation splits and evaluation unchanged.
